_comment: The whole chain in one fixture: package.json declares lodash as a range, the committed lock resolves it to 4.17.21, and the add-on ships the library. The lock's pin is what names a release, the release's published listing is what the shipped bytes are matched against, and the match is what puts the dependency in front of the OSV audit - so vendor-vulnerable rejects. Nothing here rests on the file's NAME: it ships as lib/collection-helpers.js, which says nothing about lodash, exactly as a real submission ships a library under the name its own build gave it. The match also makes the file vendored, so the source scanners leave it alone. Its sibling package-range-locked pins the offline half, that a resolving lock silences both lock checks.
